investigations.label: depth_1
investigations.text: The graph returned this evidence path: ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477. Review the transfer evidence before deciding. These connections do not establish laundering; a named analyst must assess them.

unsupported_claims: The thesis only asserts a shared-device link (ACC-4471 to DEV-f31c to ACC-10477) and explicitly disclaims laundering, so it doesn't claim more than the evidence shows.

The evidence suggests a pattern (7 inbound transfers of ~11M each in rapid succession, followed by outbound 11M to ACC-10477 and 55M to ACC-3), but nothing in the thesis or actions asserts or acts on it.
No pending actions are proposed, so there is nothing to validate beyond the existence of the device link.
missing_queries: Profile ACC-10477 and ACC-3 (counterparty types, in/out sums, onward flows) to see whether funds continue downstream.
Check shared-identifier history for DEV-f31c: when it was linked to each account and whether other accounts use it.
Establish baseline activity for ACC-4471 to determine whether the burst of near-identical inbound amounts is anomalous.

unsupported_claims: The thesis only asserts graph connectivity (shared device/person links) and explicitly disclaims laundering, so no laundering conclusion is established by the rows.
Shared-identifier hops to ACC-1 and ACC-55820 are inferred paths with no transfer rows tying funds along DEV-f31c/DEV-r00-1 links.
missing_queries: Full transfer history for ACC-10477, ACC-1 and ACC-55820 to test whether funds actually moved along the shared-identifier path
Timing/velocity analysis of the near-simultaneous ~11M inbound credits versus the 55M outbound to ACC-3
Device and person attributes for DEV-f31c, DEV-r00-1 and PER-2291 (account counts, legitimacy of sharing)

investigations.label: memory
investigations.text: The most recent prior finding on ACC-4471 was learned at 1792249903 (author agent, reviewed: no, confidence medium). It recorded the path ACC-4471 → DEV-f31c → ACC-10477 → DEV-r00-1 → ACC-1, and its linked hold proposal was denied. An earlier finding learned at 1792249875 with the same path is reviewed: yes, and its escalate action was approved; this is an observed shared-identifier path, not proof of laundering. CASH and XB rails are rail_not_ingested, so absence of evidence there is not evidence of absence.

unsupported_claims: The thesis cites a hold proposal denied and an escalate action approved, but no evidence rows contain any action or approval/denial records; these cannot be verified.
The claim that the most recent finding is 'reviewed: no, confidence medium' is supported for reviewed (false) but confidence is not present in the rows.
The statement that CASH and XB rails are rail_not_ingested is not backed by any row; no rail-coverage evidence is shown.
missing_queries: Fetch the action/proposal records (hold denied, escalate approved) linked to findings 13422a79 and 50d76508.
Query ingestion status for CASH and XB rails.
Verify the DEV-f31c and DEV-r00-1 device-sharing edges directly, since path hops through them appear only as path_ids.
